answer: The network issues each identity a random render seed. The agent must render a fixed 3D scene with a tundra biome, an umber material, and a mesh with a vertex count of at least one million, then submit the image hash. Nodes re-render the same deterministic scene and compare the hash. A copied or cached image fails because the seed changes every epoch. A sybil therefore needs a separate GPU render per identity, so k fakes cost k times the GPU hours and memory. Honest agents reuse their renderer and hardware. An attacker cannot amortize one render across many identities.
